organization.name: Perth Racing
organization.short_description:
Perth Racing is the leading thoroughbred racing club in Western Australia, operating under the historic Western Australian Turf Club, which was established in 1848. The club manages two prominent racecourses: Ascot Racecourse, known as the "grand old lady" of Australian racecourses, and Belmont Park Racecourse, which hosts events primarily during the winter season.

Perth Racing organizes around 90 to 100 race meetings each year, featuring major events like the Perth Cup and the Quokka. The club also provides race day hospitality options and hosts non-raceday events such as corporate functions and weddings. It serves a diverse audience, including horse racing enthusiasts, corporate clients, and tourists, making it a central hub for racing and events in the region. With a commitment to enhancing its facilities, Perth Racing continues to play a significant role in the local community and the racing industry.

organization.name: Racing Victoria Group
organization.short_description:
Racing Victoria Group, based in Docklands, Melbourne, is the governing body for thoroughbred horse racing in Victoria, Australia. Established on December 17, 2001, it operates as a non-profit organization with a mission to promote and develop the sport. The Group manages racing across 67 tracks and operates 363 days a year, generating significant economic impact for the state.

The organization comprises three main entities: Racing Victoria, which oversees governance; Racing.com Media, responsible for live broadcasting and digital content; and Thoroughbred Racing Productions, which handles video and event production. Racing Victoria Group provides essential services such as industry regulation, race scheduling, and integrity monitoring, while also supporting education and marketing initiatives to engage the community and attract spectators. With a vision of "Racing for All," the Group aims to enhance the experience of all participants in the racing ecosystem.

Perth Racing is the leading thoroughbred racing club in Western Australia, operating under the historic Western Australian Turf Club, which was established in 1848. The club manages two prominent racecourses: Ascot Racecourse, known as the "grand old lady" of Australian racecourses, and Belmont Park Racecourse, which hosts events primarily during the winter season.

Perth Racing organizes around 90 to 100 race meetings each year, featuring major events like the Perth Cup and the Quokka. The club also provides race day hospitality options and hosts non-raceday events such as corporate functions and weddings. It serves a diverse audience, including horse racing enthusiasts, corporate clients, and tourists, making it a central hub for racing and events in the region. With a commitment to enhancing its facilities, Perth Racing continues to play a significant role in the local community and the racing industry.

additionalDescriptions:
The Western Australian Turf Club (now operating as Perth Racing) has embarked on an impressive transformation and redevelopment, signalling an exciting new chapter for racing, tourism and events in Perth. 

Perth Racing, which manages two tracks - Ascot Racecourse and Belmont Park - is a club that never sleeps. As Western Australia's only metropolitan club, Perth Racing hosts a busy 90 meetings per season, as well as non-raceday events.

Ascot Racecourse is more than just a race track; it's also a training facility. More than 500 horses are put through their preliminary paces on the Ascot Racecourse gallops during a typical week and the venue has played an important role in the development of several champions, including two-time WS Cox Plate winner Northerly, the Fighting Tiger of whom there is an imposing statue next to the venue's Flametree Lawn. Belmont Park is located within a torpedo punt of the new Perth Stadium that officially opened on 21 January 2018.

For seven years, Sir Ernest Lee-Steere combined being Chairman of the Western Australian Turf Club with holding the equally prestigious office of the Lord Mayor of Perth and it was on his watch that the racing organisation relaid the Belmont Park surface, transforming it into one of the world's best wet-weather tracks.

organization.short_description:
Perth Racing is the leading thoroughbred racing club in Western Australia, operating under the historic Western Australian Turf Club, which was established in 1848. The club manages two prominent racecourses: Ascot Racecourse, known as the "grand old lady" of Australian racecourses, and Belmont Park Racecourse, which hosts events primarily during the winter season.

Perth Racing organizes around 90 to 100 race meetings each year, featuring major events like the Perth Cup and the Quokka. The club also provides race day hospitality options and hosts non-raceday events such as corporate functions and weddings. It serves a diverse audience, including horse racing enthusiasts, corporate clients, and tourists, making it a central hub for racing and events in the region. With a commitment to enhancing its facilities, Perth Racing continues to play a significant role in the local community and the racing industry.

additionalDescriptions:
The Western Australian Turf Club (now operating as Perth Racing) has embarked on an impressive transformation and redevelopment, signalling an exciting new chapter for racing, tourism and events in Perth. 

Perth Racing, which manages two tracks - Ascot Racecourse and Belmont Park - is a club that never sleeps. As Western Australia's only metropolitan club, Perth Racing hosts a busy 90 meetings per season, as well as non-raceday events.

Ascot Racecourse is more than just a race track; it's also a training facility. More than 500 horses are put through their preliminary paces on the Ascot Racecourse gallops during a typical week and the venue has played an important role in the development of several champions, including two-time WS Cox Plate winner Northerly, the Fighting Tiger of whom there is an imposing statue next to the venue's Flametree Lawn. Belmont Park is located within a torpedo punt of the new Perth Stadium that officially opened on 21 January 2018.

Perth Racing's head office, Lee-Steere House, is located opposite Ascot Racecourse. The Grandstand Road premises honour the contribution of the Lee-Steere family. Sir Ernest Augustus Lee-Steere was Chairman of the Western Australian Turf Club from 1919 to 1940 and Sir Ernest Lee-Steere was Chairman of the Western Australian Turf Club from 1963 to 1984. For seven years, Sir Ernest Lee-Steere combined being Chairman of the Western Australian Turf Club with holding the equally prestigious office of the Lord Mayor of Perth and it was on his watch that the racing organisation relaid the Belmont Park surface, transforming it into one of the world's best wet-weather tracks.
